content:
Riley M: hey everyone, day 1 and i'm stuck. i completed the Okta SSO flow on my phone (Okta Verify push accepted) but Google Workspace still shows 'Account not provisioned'. Also trying to register my YubiKey for MFA but Okta errors with 'webauthn: authenticator not recognized'. any ideas?

Marie (IT): welcome Riley! can you confirm the exact email used for Okta? and are you using a personal laptop or the company Mac? sometimes org units need manual fix.

Riley M: using riley.m@redwood.ai, personal MacBook Air (M2). clicked the welcome invite at 09:06.

Nora (People Ops): i submitted the new-hire batch at 08:50 so provisioning should be complete. i'll check.

Marie (IT): looking at the admin console now 1: the user exists but the Drive license didn't attach because the provisioning worker hit a transient quota error. i've retried the job. try signing out of all Google accounts or use an incognito window to force the SSO prompt.

Riley M: signed out and tried incognito, still says 'Account pending provisioning'. any way to force-refresh?

Carlos (DevEx): pinging in case of 1Password/CLI overlap. Riley, are you also trying `op signin`? sometimes the 1Password/Okta browser flow can interfere with the Google SSO if you have existing sessions.

Riley M: not yet, just focused on Google + YubiKey for now.

Marie (IT): i triggered a manual license assign and cleared stale Okta sessions for riley.m@redwood.ai. that should force the provisioning. give it ~2 minutes and retry. also FYI the invite link can sometimes land you in the wrong org if you have multiple Google accounts in the browser.

Riley M: after 3 mins it worked! i can access Gmail now but shared drives aren't visible yet. also tried YubiKey registration and this time Okta failed with:

```
webauthn error: NotAllowedError: The operation was aborted by the user agent or the platform
```
I'm definitely touching the key when prompted.

Carlos (DevEx): on macOS, if you have Touch ID enabled and you're using a USB-C YubiKey with an adapter, the OS sometimes interprets it specially. couple quick checks: 1) try a different USB port or hub; 2) open chrome://flags and ensure WebAuthn is enabled (usually default); 3) test registration on a company laptop if possible. Also try using Firefox which has a different WebAuthn stack.

Marie (IT): also check System Preferences -> Security & Privacy -> Privacy -> Input Monitoring / Files and Folders for the browser 1 sometimes Chrome needs permission to access USB devices. macOS can block WebAuthn flows if permissions are strict.

Riley M: i tried Firefox and got farther; Okta prompted for the device and then showed a spinner, then an error: 'authenticator not recognized (0x6b)'. plugged key into the other USB-C port and now it registered. weird but success. thanks!

Carlos (DevEx): awesome. one more thing: if you plan to use the 1Password CLI, that can race with browser SSO. if you hit `state_mismatch` or `polling timed out` run:

```
op signin redwood --raw
# then
eval $(op signin redwood --raw)
```
That tends to bypass the local redirect listener.

Riley M: good to know. any outstanding access I should check? i still don't see the infra GitHub repo. i got an invite but clicking it shows 'You don't have access'.

Nora (People Ops): GitHub team invites are handled separately. Riley, can you DM me your GitHub handle so i can escalate to infra?

Riley M: sent DM (rileym-dev).

AccessBot: Onboarding status: Riley M 1 of 6 tasks completed (Google Workspace, MFA enrolled) at 2026-03-26 14:04 UTC.

Marie (IT): added you to the eng-docs shared drive and re-sent the GitHub invite to the org admin. once you accept the repo invite, try a git clone. if it still says denied, open this thread and tag @Marie (IT).

Riley M: clone worked after the re-invite, and 1Password CLI signin behaves with the --raw trick. everything green now. thanks team :tada:
